decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display is a core, made-to-order format that costs almost nothing to keep in the catalog, so the option is still worth holding.
The pegboard-back shelf display is close to the core offer and has low carrying cost, but it is a niche variant among many similar options.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a staple of point-of-sale business with minimal cost to offer, so there is no reason to give up the option.
The eighth-pallet display fills a common size slot at low cost, and its value has not been shown to fail.
The wooden pallet departs from the cardboard core and needs separate materials and handling, which raises its carrying cost, but with no clear evidence of failure the option is still kept.
Physical media retail is shrinking, so this option's value is resolving unfavorably, yet keeping a cardboard variant that can be adapted to other uses costs little.
